title: Masters (Msc) Applied ICT in Public Health (MPH)
text:
MASTER IN :

APPLIED ICT IN PUBLIC HEALTH

APPLY NOW

Master

MSc in Applied ICT in Public Health
At the world's most consequential intersection: where digital technology meets human health. A pioneering program creating professionals who understand epidemiology and health systems as deeply as databases and networks — and who can deploy technology to save lives at population scale.
Apply now See the outcomes

At a glance
Degree Master of Science
Faculty ICT
Delivery Online or onsite
Language English or French
Sector growth +28%
Market by 2034 $2.3 trillion

Program objectives

The curriculum grounds you in the core sciences of public health — fundamental theories, epidemiology, healthcare systems, and infectious, communicable and non-communicable diseases — then equips you with the digital instruments transforming them: health management information systems and telemedicine, e-reproductive, maternal and child health, e-global health, data mining in public health, and the modelling and simulation of disease. Courses in health project management, e-healthcare management, the anthropology of health, and quantitative and qualitative research analysis complete a truly interdisciplinary preparation.

Public health theory Epidemiology Healthcare systems Communicable diseases Non-communicable diseases Health information systems Telemedicine e-Maternal & child health e-Global health Data mining in public health Disease modelling Anthropology of health

Learning outcomes

Design and manage health information systems
The backbone of any functioning health service.

Deploy telemedicine to remote communities
Where the distance to a clinic is the diagnosis.

Mine health data to detect outbreaks
And target interventions where they change outcomes.

Model epidemics to guide policy
Simulation that ministries can act on.

Manage health-technology projects
From proposal through to evaluation.

Work across disciplines
An internship in a real health organisation, plus a network.

Integration in society

Digital health is rewriting what is possible in medicine and public health — and nowhere more dramatically than in Africa, where telemedicine already reaches 52% more rural patients and mobile health could serve 650 million people. Health informaticians close the distance between clinics and communities, give ministries real-time epidemic intelligence, and stretch scarce health budgets further. Your work will directly advance universal health coverage, maternal and child survival, and epidemic preparedness.

Combine compassion with computation — and build the systems that heal nations.

Employment opportunities and careers

The digital health market is expanding fast — projected to grow from roughly $492 billion in 2026 to over $2.3 trillion by 2034 at a 21.6% annual rate, with Africa's own market expanding rapidly. Employment of health services managers, including health informatics specialists, is projected to grow 28% — among the fastest of any profession. Employers include ministries of health, hospitals, NGOs, WHO and UN agencies, health-tech startups and research institutes.

Mission Statement

The mission of the faculty is to offer programs at undergraduate and graduate levels, which develop and produce managers and other business professionals capable of using human and other resources to meet development needs and take advantage of the opportunities of Cameroon within the global context.

Objectives of the Faculty

The general objective of the faculty is to develop and offer academic programs for the development of the intellectual and managerial potentials of its students. Specific objectives are:

Intellectual & managerial potential
To provide knowledge that develops the students' intellectual and managerial potentials.

Critical thinking & enterprise
To develop students' intellectual and critical thinking ability as well as their managerial and entrepreneurial skills.

Information for decision-making
To foster the ability to organize, analyze and interpret information for decision making.

High moral standards
To instil high moral standards of personal and professional behaviour, consistent with positions of trust and leadership in society.

Efficiency & integrity
To imbue in students sensitivity and commitment to efficiency in the use of resources as well as to integrity, accountability and transparency.

Curiosity & new knowledge
To encourage and develop a sense of curiosity and inquiry needed for innovative thinking and the development of new knowledge.

Opportunities Opened to B.Sc. Graduates

After gaining the Bachelor Degrees, students will have a world of opportunities available to them.

Further training & education
Progress to the Master's and Ph.D. programs of the University while working, securing lucrative jobs and studying simultaneously.

Progression to universities worldwide
With recognition at universities around the world, the BSc is truly a passport to global opportunities.

Professional qualifications globally
Progression to AAT, ACCA, AIA, CIMA, CPA, CIB, CIM, CIPFA, CII and more — with exemptions that let students qualify much faster.

Career Opportunities

With its focus on practical skills and knowledge, the B.Sc. programs prepare students for a fast-paced career in the world of business and related fields. Students will gain real-life work experience to complement their academic knowledge and to make them stand out in the competitive job markets.

The opportunities to participate in internships allow students to put their new knowledge and abilities to practice in the real world. Gaining strong work experience with leading organizations will help set students apart from the competition, allowing them to achieve their career goals much quicker. When coupled with comprehensive career support from workshops that will be organized, students will quickly see their career potentials increase — benefiting from individual career advice, seminars, workshops, mock interviews, resume surgery and more.

Graduation Requirements

In order to earn a B.Sc. in any of the disciplines, students are expected to earn a total of at least 240 credits, pass all compulsory courses and University requirements, have a GPA of at least 2.00, and be of good conduct. For full-time students the program should not exceed two and a half or three years for an honours degree; for part-time students, not more than four years.

Assessment of Students

Students shall be assessed for their academic performance in examinations. Students shall be declared successful when they pass all the compulsory courses and obtain a Cumulative GPA of at least 2.00 on 4.00. The grading is distributed as follows:

30% Continuous assessment
70% Examination
80% Mandatory class attendance
2.00 Minimum Cumulative GPA

Industrial Experience & Internship
All students will be required to do an internship of 256 hours (two months), evaluated by the field supervisor (30%), the internship report (50%) and the academic supervisor (20%). English is the main language of instruction, and every student must pass four credits in a second language to qualify for graduation from the Faculty.
